Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of SVG103 (Paxalisib) in Focal Cortical Dysplasia Type II (FCD-II), Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) or Hemimegalencephaly (HME)

drafts.email1:
Hi Guido,

I came across NCT07322887 — your Phase 2 study of SUL-238 (1500 mg t.i.d.) film-coated tablets, SUL-238 (500 mg t.i.d.) film-coated tablets in Parkinson's Disease (PD), and wanted to reach out.

Phase 2 is where the exposure-response relationship defines the program's trajectory — a robust E-R model at this stage directly supports the Phase 3 dose rationale and significantly reduces regulatory back-and-forth. With 45 patients, you have a limited dataset due to small cohort size — but Bayesian PopPK/E-R and simulation-based dose optimization help you build a defensible Phase 3 dose rationale even with sparse data, which is exactly what FDA expects in these scenarios. For SUL-238 (1500 mg t.i.d.) film-coated tablets, SUL-238 (500 mg t.i.d.) film-coated tablets, getting this analysis right now avoids costly protocol amendments downstream.

Our team at PumasAI — pharmacometricians and clinical pharmacologists, several with prior experiences from from FDA, Novartis, and BMS — has delivered 40+ regulatory submissions across FDA, EMA, PMDA, and Health Canada, all accepted on first review. We handle the full clinical pharmacology program end-to-end: PopPK, exposure-response, dose optimization, clinical trial simulation, and regulatory writing through submission.

Would a short call make sense to see if there's a fit?
